product_offering.core_offering: Unit provides an API-first embedded finance platform that enables software companies to embed banking, card issuing, payments, and lending products (accounts, wallets, cards, money movement, capital) into their own applications in 3-6 weeks. It operates as middleware between U.S. bank partners and software platforms, offering two implementation paths: Ready-to-Launch (fully managed, single-line-of-code integration) and Custom (full API control). Unit handles compliance, KYC/AML, and regulatory infrastructure so platforms can offer FDIC-insured banking, branded cards, and embedded lending under their own brand.
product_offering.differentiator: Multi-bank partner model providing resilience and regulatory flexibility; API-first architecture enabling rapid embedded finance deployment; enterprise-grade security certifications (SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS Level 1); end-to-end compliance orchestration; combination of managed Ready-to-Launch and custom API integration paths.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Enables software platforms to embed accounts, cards, lending, and payments within weeks through APIs without obtaining a banking charter. Platforms gain new revenue streams from interchange, interest, and transaction fees. Customers experience branded financial products within their existing software workflows. Unit handles compliance, bank relationships, and infrastructure complexity.
product_offering.problem_solved: Software companies need to embed financial products (banking, cards, lending, payments) into their platforms to generate new revenue streams, increase customer lifetime value, and reduce churn — but lack the regulatory expertise, banking relationships, and technical infrastructure to build these products themselves. Traditional banks are too slow and inflexible for modern software companies. Unit solves this by providing API-based embedded finance infrastructure backed by multiple bank partners, enabling platforms to launch financial products in 3-6 weeks instead of 2-3 years.
quantifiable_outcome: 4x higher customer lifetime value for platforms embedding banking products (Roofstock case study)
50% lower customer acquisition costs for embedded banking users (Baselane case study)
7x transaction volume growth over six months prior to May 2022 Series C
Platform serves 800,000+ individuals, 300,000+ contractors, and 200,000+ small businesses
product_offering.product_overview: Unit is an embedded finance platform offering a modular architecture with two primary implementation paths: Ready-to-Launch (fully managed, single-line-of-code integration) and Custom (API-based, full control). The platform provides four core building blocks: Accounts & Wallets (FBO accounts and digital wallets), Money Movement (ACH, wire, check, real-time payments), Card Issuing (debit, credit, charge cards), and Capital (merchant cash advances, lines of credit, credit cards). These building blocks serve three customer segments: Businesses (capital, banking, expenses), Independent Workers (instant payouts, wallets, cards), and Consumers (balances, cards, money movement). The platform processed over $80 billion in annual transactions across 5 million accounts with 12 million daily API calls.

icp.description: Primary ICP. Unit sells embedded finance infrastructure to vertical SaaS, marketplace, and B2B software platforms (e.g., Wix, RentSpree, Relay, Roofstock, Baselane, Worldpay) seeking to monetize their user base with banking, card, lending, and payment products. Buyers are engineering and product leaders who lack the regulatory expertise and bank-partner relationships to build financial infrastructure themselves. Decision dynamics are enterprise sales-led with demos, sandbox evaluation, and contract negotiation; sales cycles range from short for self-serve Ready-to-Launch to multi-month for Custom integrations. Pain points include the cost and time (2-3 years) of building financial infrastructure in-house, compliance complexity (KYC/AML, banking regulations), and the need to increase customer LTV and revenue per user.

profiles.name: Itai Damti
profiles.overview: Co-founder and CEO of Unit, leading the company's embedded finance strategy and vision.
profiles.profile_commentary: Itai Damti is the co-founder and CEO of Unit, the New York-based embedded finance platform. He is described as the visionary leader driving the company's strategy of enabling software companies to embed financial products via APIs. He co-founded the company and leads it alongside CTO Doron Somech and CPO Ehud Fisher, raising $151M+ in disclosed funding from Insight Partners, Accel, and Better Tomorrow Ventures to reach a $1.2 billion unicorn valuation in May 2022.

profiles.name: Doron Somech
profiles.overview: Co-founder and CTO of Unit, leading the platform's technical architecture and engineering organization.
profiles.profile_commentary: Doron Somech co-founded Unit and serves as its Chief Technology Officer. He oversees the engineering organization that built Unit's API-first embedded finance platform on AWS infrastructure, which today handles 12M+ daily API calls and $80B+ in annual transaction volume. His leadership spans platform development, payment-rail integration (Federal Reserve, Visa card networks), and multi-bank partner orchestration. He works from the company's Tel Aviv engineering hub.

profiles.name: Ehud Fisher
profiles.overview: Chief Product Officer at Unit, overseeing product strategy and development for the embedded finance platform.
profiles.profile_commentary: Ehud Fisher is Unit's Chief Product Officer, leading product strategy and development across the company's accounts, payments, cards, and capital offerings. He is part of the founding leadership team alongside CEO Itai Damti and CTO Doron Somech.

recent_move.description: Closed a $100M Series C led by Insight Partners at a $1.2B post-money valuation, with Accel, Aleph, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Flourish Ventures, Karman Ventures, and StepStone Group participating, to accelerate product development, expand into credit products, and strengthen compliance and legal teams.

Launched Wix Checking with Wix to deliver integrated business banking for Wix Payments users, representing one of Unit's largest named flagship platform partnerships and validating its enterprise readiness.

Expanded bank-partner network with Vantage Bank and Lincoln Savings Bank partnerships (alongside Thread Bank) to provide multi-bank resilience, regulatory flexibility, and a Business Continuity Tool for bank partners managing fintech program failures.

Expanded product surface into Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable solutions and additional capital products (cash advances, invoice factoring, term loans, revolving lines of credit) to capture more wallet share within embedded SMB customers.

Launched embedded banking for RentSpree (rental technology platform with ~4M users), enabling FDIC-insured interest-earning accounts up to 2.75% APY for small landlords and expanding Unit's footprint in PropTech.

Unit Labs partnered with Hyperliquid Strategies Inc to launch a validator node on the Hyperliquid blockchain, with HYPE tokens custodied at Anchorage Digital Bank, signaling an exploratory move into institutional digital-asset infrastructure.

expansion_highlight.description: In 2025 Unit announced expansion into Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable products and additional capital products (cash advances, invoice factoring, term loans, revolving lines of credit), extending wallet share within embedded SMB customers beyond accounts and cards.

2024-2026 partnership cadence shows vertical expansion into PropTech (RentSpree), payments and e-commerce platforms (Wix, Worldpay), and SMB banking/accounting (Relay, Homebase, Honeybook), broadening beyond early real-estate and freelance segments.

Multi-bank strategy via Vantage Bank, Lincoln Savings Bank, and Thread Bank — including a Business Continuity Tool for bank partners — deepens resilience and reduces single-bank concentration risk, a key BaaS industry concern post-2023 partner-bank failures.

Unit Labs' May 2026 validator-node partnership with Hyperliquid Strategies on the Hyperliquid blockchain (with Anchorage Digital Bank custody) signals a tentative international and digital-asset infrastructure expansion beyond its U.S.-domiciled core.

Headcount of 101-250 across NYC and Tel Aviv, plus dedicated roles including CFO (Vignesh Nathan), Chief Legal Officer (Alex Acree), Head of Compliance (Paula Harris), SVP Customer Success (Kate Levin), VP Marketing (Louise Ng), and VP Sales (Jeremy Bass), indicates investment in commercial scaling and regulated-finance readiness.

Total disclosed equity funding of ~$169M across five rounds (seed through Series C, 2019-2022) culminating in a $1.2B post-money valuation provides a multi-year runway to pursue product and partnership expansion without near-term fundraising pressure.
